plan.universeTitle: Economic Indicators and Scholarly Output: A Cross-Domain View
plan.summary: This information universe provides a focused view of recent US economic trends alongside a curated selection of scholarly publications and their citation relationships. It integrates monthly observations of the Consumer Price Index and unemployment rates, presenting them both as time series and as discrete economic observation objects. Complementing this, metadata for research articles and books from Crossref are included, allowing for a 'publication-canopy' and 'object-grove' visualization of scholarly output. A derived dataset further maps the citation network between research articles, revealing the relational geometry of academic influence. All data spans a recent one-year window, preserving original numeric values, units, and provenance, while highlighting key derivations.

datasets.title: US Consumer Price Index: Monthly Trends
datasets.interpretation: This dataset presents the US Consumer Price Index (all items, not seasonally adjusted) as a time series of monthly numeric observations. Each record includes the index value and its unit (index, 1982–84=100), reflecting changes in consumer prices over time. The data originates from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) and covers a specific period, allowing for the visualization of its progression and magnitude.

datasets.title: US Civilian Unemployment Rate: Monthly Fluctuations
datasets.interpretation: This dataset displays the US civilian unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted) as a time series of monthly numeric observations. Each record provides the unemployment percentage, indicating labor market conditions. The data is sourced from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) and offers a view of the rate's fluctuations and overall trend within the specified timeframe, preserving its original unit of 'percent'.

datasets.title: Aggregated US Economic Observations: CPI and Unemployment
datasets.interpretation: This dataset represents individual monthly economic observations as distinct objects. It is derived by losslessly wrapping the retained CPI and unemployment observations, preserving their original numeric values, units, and provenance. Each object encapsulates a single economic data point, allowing for a visualization that emphasizes the discrete nature and attributes of each observation rather than a continuous trend.

datasets.title: Crossref Research Articles: Publication Canopy
datasets.interpretation: This dataset contains metadata for research articles sourced from Crossref, representing a 'publication-canopy' of scholarly output. Each record details a specific article, including its Digital Object Identifier (DOI) and publication date. The visualization emphasizes the collective body of research, allowing for exploration of publication patterns and the distribution of scholarly works over time.

datasets.title: Crossref Book Metadata: Object Grove of Publications
datasets.interpretation: This dataset provides metadata for books from Crossref, visualized as an 'object-grove.' Each record represents a distinct book, identified by its Digital Object Identifier (DOI) and publication date. The geometry of this dataset emphasizes individual book entities, allowing for an examination of their attributes and distribution within the collection, distinct from a continuous series or network.

datasets.title: Crossref Citation Network: Research Article References
datasets.interpretation: This dataset represents a citation network, derived from the deposited DOI references within the research-crossref dataset. Each record signifies a directed edge from a citing DOI to a referenced DOI, illustrating the relational geometry of academic citations. The visualization focuses on the connections and pathways of scholarly influence, where external targets are represented by their identifiers.
